stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A luminous object AB sits in front of a converging lens of known focal length $f' = 10\,\text{cm}$. Drag the screen along the bench until the image of AB looks sharp. Read $p$ (object $\to$ lens) and $p'$ (lens $\to$ screen) in the HUD, and watch $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{p'}$ collapse onto $\frac{1}{f'}$.
stages.concept: Descartes' conjugation formula: $\frac{1}{\overline{OA'}} - \frac{1}{\overline{OA}} = \frac{1}{f'}$. Using positive bench distances $p = |\overline{OA}|$ and $p' = |\overline{OA'}|$, this becomes $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{p'} = \frac{1}{f'}$. Focometry = measure $p$ and $p'$, compute $f'$.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: Three lenses of unknown focal length are handed to you, one after the other. For each: slide the screen to find the sharp image, then press FIRE (or Space) to record your measurement. You have 5 shots to lock in all 3 focal lengths.
stages.concept: Sharp-screen protocol: at the sharp position, $p'$ satisfies $\frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{p'} = \frac{1}{f'}$. Since $p$ is fixed and known, one measured $p'$ yields $f' = \frac{p \cdot p'}{p + p'}$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: No sharpness bar, no rays — only a blurred image projected on the screen. Trust your eye: place the screen where the image looks sharpest, then FIRE to submit. One shot per lens, three lenses. Miss any, and the whole setup resets.
stages.concept: You measure $p'$ from the sharp position, then compute $f' = \dfrac{p \cdot p'}{p + p'}$ (with $p = 30\,\text{cm}$ fixed). Peek shows the current $p'$ readout and the plugged-in $f'$ so you can verify your paper arithmetic.

labels.tip1: drag the screen — sharp image = image plane hit
labels.tip2: aim the screen, then SPACE to record f'
labels.tip3: eye the sharpest blur, then FIRE — one shot per lens

1.1: Slide the screen left and right; the image sharpens then blurs.
1.2: At the sharp position, the ray triangle closes onto the screen. Read p and p' from the HUD.
1.3: Verify: with p = 30 cm and p' at the sharp position, 1/p + 1/p' should equal 1/10 cm⁻¹.

2.1: For each lens, the object is still at p = 30 cm. Only p' changes.
2.2: Slide the screen until the arrow on it is crisp, then Fire to lock the measurement.
2.3: Shorter f' → image forms closer to the lens. Watch the sharpness bar peak; that's your p'.

3.1: No sharpness readout — read the blurred image on the screen. The sharpest position minimizes the blob size.
3.2: Move the screen slowly. Overshoot each direction to bracket the sharp spot, then land in the middle.
3.3: Peek reveals your current p' and the f' it implies via f' = p·p'/(p+p'). Compare with your paper estimate before firing.
